FreeRelay is not a gateway, a proxy, or a router. It is an inference operating system. The distinction is not semantic. A gateway forwards. An OS governs. FreeRelay governs every decision about how inference gets executed — before, during, and after the model call — and it learns from every outcome to make the next decision better.
Five pillars separate it from everything that exists:
Profile requests on 10 axes before touching a provider. Know that this is a deep-reasoning multilingual coding task with strict JSON output before choosing anything.
Learn P(success | workload, provider, config) from real traffic. Route on expected utility, not static capability metadata.
Static scoring formula. Round-robin with health checks.
Execute declarative multi-model DAGs. Fan out, verify, repair, judge. Return a validated response with full provenance.
Send one request to one provider. Return whatever comes back.
Validate every output structurally and semantically. Repair before returning. Make output quality transactional.
Hope the model got it right.
Split brain from hot path. Policy as code. Experiments. Tenant isolation. Deep observability. Operational ownership.
A YAML config file and a dashboard nobody reads.

The real moat is not features. It is the feedback loop: every request makes the next routing decision slightly better. Over millions of requests, FreeRelay develops an empirical model of provider behavior that no static documentation can replicate.
2.1 The Split: Control Plane vs Data Plane

This split is the single most consequential architectural decision. It must be made on Day 1. Retrofitting it after the fact requires a full rewrite. The rule is absolute: the control plane never touches a live request. The data plane never makes a policy decision.

Every component communicates through exactly one of three mechanisms. No exceptions. Mixing mechanisms is an architecture violation.
Redis Streams — async, append-only, ordered: outcome records from data plane to control plane. Retention: 7 days. Consumer group: control-plane-learner.
Redis Pub/Sub — async, broadcast, no persistence: policy updates from control plane to all data plane workers. Channel: freerelay:policy:v2.

Redis Hash/Sorted Set — synchronous reads: capability registry, circuit breaker state, budget state, bandit arm weights. All reads by data plane. All writes by control plane or via atomic Lua scripts.

⚑ Data plane workers NEVER write to capability registry, bandit weights, or policy objects. They write ONLY to: (1) the outcome stream, (2) circuit breaker state via Lua CAS script, (3) budget counters via Lua INCRBY script. Everything else is control plane territory.

The profiler runs on the hot path and must complete in under 5ms for p99. It uses no LLM calls. It uses no network calls. It is a pure local computation pipeline. Every axis is determined by one of three methods: rule-based heuristics, a pre-loaded sklearn logistic regression model (fitted offline), or client-supplied headers.

After all axes are determined, the profiler computes a confidence score (0.0–1.0) representing how reliable the profile is. Low confidence triggers conservative routing (prefer proven providers over exploration).
def compute_confidence(profile: WorkloadProfile, classifier_proba: float) -> float:
score *= 0.9 # complex tool graphs → profiler less reliable
score *= 0.85 # very long context → harder to classify
return max(0.3, min(1.0, score)) # floor at 0.3 — never route blind

⚑ When confidence < 0.5, the router disables UCB exploration (ucb_bonus = 0) and routes to the historically safest provider for the detected task_family. Exploration is a privilege of confident profiling.

The profiler ships with 120 labeled test cases covering edge cases across all 10 axes. CI fails if accuracy drops below 0.92 on any axis. Test cases are stored in tests/profiler/labeled_requests.jsonl and regenerated quarterly from production traffic (with human review).
5. Routing Engine — Expected Utility & UCB Math

Every available provider-model pair receives a score. The pair with the highest score is selected. 'Available' means: circuit state is CLOSED or HALF_OPEN, AND budget_score > 0, AND tenant policy score is 1.0.

6. DAG Execution Engine — Full Runtime Spec

The DAG engine is an async Python runtime that executes directed acyclic graphs of inference steps. It is the core of what makes FreeRelay an orchestration platform rather than a gateway. The engine is deterministic: given the same workflow definition and the same model outputs, it always produces the same execution trace.
Step graph is parsed from YAML at startup and compiled into a Python dependency graph (dict[step_id, set[dependency_ids]]).
At execution time, steps with no unresolved dependencies are dispatched immediately via asyncio.create_task.
As steps complete, dependent steps are unblocked and dispatched. This is a topological traversal with async concurrency at each frontier.
Step outputs are stored in an ExecutionContext dict, keyed by step_id. Downstream steps read their inputs from this context.
Conditional steps evaluate their condition against the context before executing. If condition is false, step is skipped and marked as skipped in the trace.
The engine enforces a global DAG timeout. If any step exceeds its per-step timeout, it is cancelled and the fallback strategy executes.
Every step execution is recorded in the ExecutionTrace, which is attached to the OutcomeRecord for full provenance.

The repair FSM is a 5-state machine. State transitions are driven by validation results and attempt counts. The FSM is deterministic: same inputs always produce the same state transitions.
States: INITIAL → VALIDATING → REPAIRING → VALIDATED | FAILED
VALIDATING + layer1_fail + attempt<4 → REPAIRING (select repair strategy)
VALIDATING + layer2_fail + attempt<4 → REPAIRING (select repair strategy)
VALIDATING + any_fail + attempt>=4 → FAILED (emit degraded response)
FAILED + fallback_available → emit best-seen response with X-FreeRelay-Validation-Status: degraded
Repair strategy selection (in order of preference):
Attempt 1: Same provider, lower temperature (0.1), explicit error in system prompt
Attempt 2: Provider with highest schema_compliance_rate for this output_contract
Attempt 3: Repair prompt (original + failed response + failures) → repair model
Attempt 4: Temperature 0.0, force_json=true, minimal tool descriptions

The anomaly detector runs in the control plane on a 5-minute tick. It computes EWMA of each latency and quality metric and flags anomalies using 3-sigma control limits. When an anomaly is detected, it immediately sets the appropriate degradation flag in the capability registry and triggers a spot benchmark run.
ewma = metric_series[-1] if metric_series else new_value
ewma_var = alpha * (new_value - ewma)**2 + (1 - alpha) * (metric_series[-2] if len(metric_series) > 1 else 0)
is_anomaly = new_value > upper_control_limit or new_value < lower_control_limit
severity = abs(new_value - ewma) / sigma if sigma > 0 else 0

To replay an agent run deterministically: load the run's routing_history and tool_output_history. For each step, instead of calling the router, return the recorded routing decision. Instead of executing tools, return the recorded tool output. Model calls are replayed against the same provider and model version where possible.

⚑ Deterministic replay requires that the provider still serves the same model version. If the provider has updated the model, replay produces a warning and uses the current model version. Full byte-for-byte determinism is not guaranteed across model updates — this is a known limitation documented in the replay API response.

Reason It Was Chosen Over Alternatives
Async-native. Automatic OpenAPI. Pydantic v2 integration. Starlette middleware composability.
Production-grade. uvloop event loop. httptools request parser. Hot reload for dev.
Async + streaming + cancellation. Timeout granularity. respx for testing. NOT aiohttp (worse API).
Rust core — 5–50x faster than v1. Strict mode. model_rebuild. NOT attrs (less ergonomic).
Official client. Async pipeline. Lua script support. Cluster support. NOT aioredis (merged).
MinHash LSH. Well-tested. Pure Python. NOT faiss (overkill, GPU dependency).
Type-safe env vars. .env file support. Nested settings. Integrates with Pydantic v2.
Standard. Full YAML 1.1 support. NOT ruamel.yaml (unnecessary complexity for this use).
CNCF standard. OTLP export. Jaeger/Grafana Tempo compatible. Vendor neutral.
De facto standard. Low overhead. Multiprocess mode for uvicorn workers.
Structured JSON. Async-safe. Context variables. Better than loguru for production.
Click wrapper with type inference. Rich integration. NOT click directly (more boilerplate).
Tables, progress, syntax highlight. The standard for Python CLI output.
OpenAI's tokenizer. cl100k_base approximates all modern LLM tokenizers within 10%.
POS tagging for instruction following validator. en_core_web_sm model (~12MB).
Salience ranking. Pure Python. Fast enough for context-size inputs.
10x faster than json for validation. Used in Layer 1 structural validator.
Benchmark scheduler in control plane. Cron + interval triggers.
httpx-native mocking. Pattern matching. Response routing. Essential for provider tests.
Python-native. Distributed. Real async load generation.
strict mode. Zero Any. disallow_untyped_defs. All code must pass before merge.
Replaces flake8+isort+pyupgrade+pydocstyle. 100x faster. One config in pyproject.toml.
Modern pyproject.toml. Editable installs. No setup.py.
Multi-stage builds. Non-root final image. Compose for local full-stack.
mypy --strict passes on every commit. Zero exceptions. Zero Any types. If a library doesn't have stubs, create a stub file in stubs/.
All function parameters and return types annotated. All class attributes annotated.
Pydantic v2 models used for all data that crosses component boundaries. No raw dicts.
TypeVar and Protocol used for generic provider interfaces — no duck typing.
Zero blocking I/O on the event loop. No time.sleep(). No requests library. No synchronous file reads in request handlers.
All provider calls use httpx async. All Redis operations use redis[asyncio]. All file operations use aiofiles if needed.
Background tasks use asyncio.create_task() with error handling. Unhandled exceptions in tasks crash silently — always add .add_done_callback(log_exception).
Semaphores used for all concurrency limits. Never raw asyncio.gather() without a limit on hot paths.
No bare except:. Every exception caught by specific type. Every except block either recovers or re-raises with added context.
Custom exception hierarchy: FreeRelayError → ProviderError / ValidationError / RoutingError / BudgetError. Never raise generic Exception.
All errors include request_id in context. Structured logging. Never print().
Provider errors always update circuit breaker and outcome record before propagating.
Unit test coverage >= 85% on core/, providers/, shared/. CI fails below this threshold.
Every provider adapter has integration tests using respx mocking. Tests cover: success, 429, 500, timeout, streaming, tool calls.
Circuit breaker state transitions tested exhaustively: all 6 transitions with concurrent request simulation.
Budget forecaster tested with synthetic time-series data covering edge cases: reset boundary, quota exhaustion mid-request, zero usage.
Profiler accuracy >= 0.92 on all 10 axes on the 120-example test set. CI runs profiler eval on every commit.
Multi-stage build: builder (install deps) → final (copy only runtime artifacts).
Final image: python:3.12-slim. No apt packages beyond what python:3.12-slim includes. Target < 200MB.
Non-root user: RUN useradd -m freerelay && USER freerelay.
Health check: HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1.
No secrets in Dockerfile or build args. All secrets via environment variables at runtime.
